title: UK fuel duty steps 52.95p to 55.95p/l as the temporary 5p cut lapses — a pre-legislated default the 2026-10-28 Budget is explicitly reserved to overrule
source: EST: THE PREFIX IS A TAXONOMY ARTIFACT ON THE RATE SCHEDULE AND AN HONEST DOUBT ABOUT WHETHER THE STEP HAPPENS AT ALL — both halves matter and they are different. RATE SCHEDULE, primary, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200 via the gov.uk content API, 21,762 bytes): gov.uk/government/publications/amended-fuel-duty-rates-for-2026-to-2027/amended-fuel-duty-rates-2026-to-2027, an HM Treasury/HMRC policy paper first published 2026-05-22T15:28:53+01:00. Its rate tables read 'Rates to 31 December 2026 | Rates from 1 January 2027 | Rates from 1 March 2027' with unleaded petrol and heavy oil (diesel) at 0.5295 / 0.5595 / 0.5795 — a 3 ppl step on 2027-01-01 and a further 2 ppl on 2027-03-01, restoring the pre-23-March-2022 rate of 57.95p. LEGAL MECHANISM, corroborated from a second and fully independent primary the same session: legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/164 (Excise Duties (Surcharges or Rebates) (Hydrocarbon Oils etc.) (Temporary Continuation of 2022 Order and Adjustments) Order 2026, made 25 February 2026) as amended by legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/555 (Amendment Order 2026, made 21 May 2026, laid 22 May 2026), both fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200). SI 2026/555 article 2 substitutes '31st December 2026' for '31st August 2026' and '1st January 2027' for '1st December 2026' throughout, so the 5p rebate expires by its own terms on 2026-12-31 and articles 8-11 (the 55.95p tier) take effect 2027-01-01 to 2027-02-28. The step therefore needs NO positive act to happen and a fresh SI to stop. THE DATE IS NOT IN DOUBT; WHETHER THE RATE MOVES IS, AND THE PUBLISHER SAYS SO ITSELF: the same gov.uk paper states verbatim 'The legislative default will be for rates to return to the levels set at Budget 2025 from 1 January 2027, but the government will confirm final rates at Budget 2026' — HM Treasury reserving the decision to the 2026-10-28 Autumn Budget (uk-autumn-budget-2026-10-28), 65 days before the step. Also filed estimate on this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix list (IR:/CAL:/BLS:/FED:/PJM:/SEC:/TSY:/OCC:/BEA:/CENSUS:/ISM:/CB:/UMICH:/FHFA:) has no slot for HM Treasury, HMRC or the UK statute book. Proposed 2026-09-09 by the uk-cpi-2026-10-21 lane; researched and made canonical by its own lane the same day
notes: RESEARCHED 2026-09-09 by its own lane (docs/research/events/uk-fuel-duty-rise-2027-01-01.md), which re-fetched every primary rather than inheriting the proposer's and added the legislation.gov.uk leg the proposal did not have. The proposal it supersedes is proposals/uk-fuel-duty-rise-2027-01-01.from-uk-cpi-2026-10-21.json, now inert; its correction of the uk-cpi-2026-09-16 lane's cancelled-1p-on-2026-09-01 claim is confirmed and carried forward. TITLE AMENDED to name this entry's whole operational content: the step is a PRE-LEGISLATED DEFAULT, not a decision, and the decision venue is dated. THE BASE RATE IS MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED, FROM THE GOVERNMENT'S OWN WEEKLY SERIES: DESNZ's weekly road fuel prices (gov.uk/government/statistics/weekly-road-fuel-prices, both CSVs fetched direct 2026-09-09, HTTP 200) carry the duty rate as a column across 1,214 consecutive weeks, 2003-06-09 to 2026-09-07. UK fuel duty last ROSE on 2011-01-03 (58.19p to 58.95p). It has not risen in 815 consecutive weeks — 15 years 8 months — and has been cut twice since (2011-03-28 to 57.95p, 2022-03-28 to 52.95p). The 5p cut's expiry has been overridden FIVE times for five, by SI every time: 2022/365 continued by 2023/329, 2024/300, 2025/228, then 2026/164, amended by 2026/555. The Excise Duties (Surcharges or Rebates) Act 1979 s.2(2) is why the pattern recurs — SI 2026/164's own explanatory note states an order 'shall cease to be in force at the expiration of a period of one year from the date on which it takes effect, unless continued in force by a further order', so 'the legislative default is a rise' has been true every year since 2022 and the rise has happened zero times. THE STATED POLICY OBJECTIVE IS STILL LIVE AND HAS INTENSIFIED: the gov.uk paper justifies the extension by 'elevated fuel prices arising from the Iran war', and since it published, UK average unleaded has gone 157.39p (w/c 2026-05-18) to 164.40p (w/c 2026-09-07), +22.9% y/y, with diesel 186.36p, +31.6% y/y — ranks 25 and 22 of 1,214 weeks — against Brent at USD 100.62, +50.9% y/y (Yahoo BZ=F, fetched 2026-09-09). SIZE, TWO WAYS, AGREEING: HM Treasury's own macroeconomic-impact line puts the Q4-2026 extension at 'reduce CPI by 0.04 percentage points'; independently, ONS's 2026 CPI weight for liquid fuels, vehicle fuels and lubricants is 27.184 parts per 1000 (series A9FS, MM23, fetched direct 2026-09-09) and 3p of duty plus 20% VAT is 3.6p on a 164.40p pump price, giving ~0.05pp. Call it 0.04-0.07pp on the January 2027 headline — half a tenth, landing in the print published ~2027-02-17 alongside the January Ofgem cap step (ofgem-price-cap-announcement-2026-11-25). AND IT IS NOT CLEANLY OBSERVABLE: the 2022 cut, worth 6.0p at the pump, showed only -3.70p at four weeks and -0.28p at eight, because crude swallowed it — measured in the same DESNZ series. IMPACT LOW. symbols: [], this repo tracks no UK-listed symbol and no house playbook is energy-, rates- or sterling-keyed; 2027-01-01 is additionally a full market closure on both sides of the Atlantic (new-years-day-market-closure-2027-01-01, sifma-uk-bond-market-closure-2027-01-01), so there is no session in which the step could be priced. NO PRICE CHANNEL IS CLAIMED. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
